system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: model serving APIs
G2: Kubernetes
G3: MLflow
G4: Airflow/Kubeflow

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Machine Learning Engineering Focus
tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110
linkedin.com/in/tmh-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with six years in analytics and data science, including over four years developing
forecasting, churn and experimentation solutions for a subscription business. Strong Python, feature
engineering and statistical evaluation, with operational batch workflows using BigQuery and Vertex
AI Workbench. Moving into machine learning engineering, bringing measurable business impact,
automated testing experience and collaboration with product, growth and data platform teams.
EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox, meal-kit subscriptions
Feb 2022 - Present
• Built a LightGBM demand forecasting model predicting weekly orders by recipe and region six
weeks ahead, with calendar, price and menu-position features. Reduced WAPE from 23% to 14%,
with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
• Run forecasting as a Vertex AI Workbench scheduled notebook, writing outputs to BigQuery for
operations to access through Looker.
• Introduced pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
• Developed an XGBoost churn model with weekly batch scoring in BigQuery to target retention
offers. Evaluation using a 10% holdout showed churn 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated
group.
• Write production SQL and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer; use dbt Cloud scheduling
and scheduled notebooks.
• Built a Streamlit sequential A/B testing calculator used by approximately 25 product and growth
colleagues. Wrote the Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment on Cloud Run.
• Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests annually, present results to leadership monthly
and delivered internal "Stats for PMs" training three times.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail
Sep 2020 - Jan 2022
• Performed customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulatory reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two
days each month.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
• Python: pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, SHAP; pytest unit testing.
• Data processing and cloud tools: SQL, BigQuery, dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, Vertex AI Workbench,
Looker.
• Engineering tools: Git version control, Jupyter, Streamlit; Dockerfile authoring for a Streamlit app.
• Modelling and evaluation: feature engineering, time-series forecasting, A/B testing, causal
inference, Bayesian statistics; R, tidyverse, brms.
SELECTED LEARNING PROJECT
Image Classification | Personal course project | 2025
• Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset, achieving approximately 80%
accuracy. Used torchvision and Google Colab; a learning project, not a production deployment.
EDUCATION
MSc Statistics, Distinction | University of the Lothians | 2020
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand
BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019
LANGUAGES
English: native | Swahili: conversational

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110
linkedin.com/in/tmh-example
Quillstone Payments
Customer Operations AI Team
Application: Machine Learning Engineer - Customer Support AI
Dear Hiring Team,
At Thistlebox, I build models that inform weekly operational decisions and evaluate whether
customer interventions work. I am applying for Quillstone Payments’ Machine Learning
Engineer - Customer Support AI role to bring that combination of Python development,
feature engineering and rigorous evaluation to your team. Your work helping merchants get
answers quickly connects practical operational outcomes with my intended move from data
science into machine learning engineering.
My demand forecasting model predicts orders by recipe and region six weeks ahead, reducing
WAPE from 23% to 14% and contributing to an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. It
runs as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook and writes results to BigQuery for
operations to use through Looker. I also developed a weekly batch-scored XGBoost churn
model; evaluation with a 10% holdout showed churn 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated
group. These projects demonstrate my experience preparing model features, building
repeatable data workflows and assessing models against business outcomes.
Alongside modelling, I write production SQL, maintain dbt models and use Git. Since 2025, I
have introduced pytest tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60%
coverage. For a Streamlit experimentation tool used by around 25 colleagues, I wrote both the
application and its Dockerfile, while the data platform team handles deployment. My delivery
experience is in scheduled and batch workflows rather than independently deployed
model-serving APIs. I would bring that practical foundation and a strong statistical
background to collaboration with your engineers, data scientists and product managers.
Quillstone’s emphasis on sharing context and learning is reflected in how I work: I present
findings to leadership monthly and have delivered "Stats for PMs" training three times. I
would welcome a conversation about how my modelling, evaluation and data-processing
experience could contribute to your customer-support AI systems as I develop further in
production ML engineering. Thank you for considering my application.
Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
